items.title: Item 1
items.text: SK Hynix Enters the U.S. Chip Race ------------------------------------- South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix is set to raise around $28 billion by launching a U.S. listing today, regulatory filings show. Each of the expected 17.79 million ADRs will represent a tenth of a common share. The move opens SK Hynix to American investors chasing soaring demand for memory chips and other semiconductors used in AI. * “It’s a good time to go and get the U.S. involved in your shares”: Daniel Morgan at Synovus Trust noted the value of the opportunity, as American investors found its Korea-only shares hard to buy – and it lets SK Hynix trade alongside rival Micron (NASDAQ:MU ), potentially closing a valuation gap. * Team Rule Breakers’ recommendation Micron up around 2% in pre-market trading: In a new $9.3 billion development, Micron broke ground on a Hiroshima cleanroom expansion on July 4, adding advanced-memory capacity for AI workloads. Management said equipment shipments should begin in 2028. Dig into Micron’s massive quarter Divider --------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 2
items.text:
AI and Chip Stocks Continue to Drive the Market -------------------------------------------------- Tech stocks once again drove markets higher last week, pushing the S&P 500 up 1.8% by Thursday’s close, with the Nasdaq gaining 2.1%. Despite some jitters creeping back in as tech stocks fell back ahead of Friday’s market closure for the July 4 weekend, Nasdaq futures rose around 1% in pre-market trading today, with S&P 500 futures up 0.4%. * WTI crude drops below $69 per barrel: Oil prices continue to fall with the Strait of Hormuz open, as the uneasy truce between the U.S. and Iran continues. The OPEC+ group of producers, meanwhile, agreed to another modest production rise for next month. * “Dancing with the devil in the pale moon light”: A post from Michael Burry on X echoed The Joker as he continued his bearish take on the AI stock boom, adding, “The AI narrative is nothing more than mass addiction.” Less theatrically, Bank of America (NYSE:BAC ) analysts said, “Our bear market signposts suggest speculation is hitting extreme levels,” and predicted a 5% drop for the S&P 500 by the end of the year. items.title: Item 3
items.text: Earnings to Watch in a Quiet Week ------------------------------------ * AZZ (NYSE:AZZ ) – recommended by Team Hidden Gems – will report its first quarter of fiscal 2027 after Wednesday’s market close. The metal coatings and industrial infrastructure specialist reported a 4.6% rise in total full-year sales across fiscal 2026, with adjusted net income up 19.3% year over year (YoY). * PepsiCo (NASDAQ:PEP ) releases Q2 earnings Thursday morning, following a 9% YoY rise in Q1 non-GAAP core EPS , from an 8.5% revenue increase. Investors should get some insight into cautious consumer spending, as the company navigates rising input cost pressures. * Delta Air Lines (NYSE:DAL ) posts Q2 results Friday, as we enter a "rare airline sweet spot" for major carriers, in the words of Bank of America analysts – high ticket prices and falling fuel costs. Q1 marked a record quarter for revenue with a 9.4% YoY rise, as non-GAAP EPS jumped 42%. Get the full lowdown on Delta's Q1 Divider -----------------------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 5
items.text: Today’s Take: When One Is All You Need ----------------------------------------- Yasser El-Shimy Ferrari (NYSE:RACE ) sells one thing: ultra-luxury sports cars. Because it owns that lane so completely, it commands years-long waiting lists and margins that make most businesses envious. That’s not a vulnerability; that’s a moat. — YASSER EL-SHIMY • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to reveal how you think about investing in businesses that depend heavily on a single product – and what can make it a feature rather than a vulnerability – or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! See more in Today’s Take Divider ------------

items.title: Item 6
items.text: Your Take ------------ FRIDAY'S TOP RESPONSE We asked: What’s a market metric or statistic from the second quarter that stood out to you, whether good, bad, or unexpected? S Member skunkfart said “Despite the S&P 500 pullback of 1% in June, the S&P 500 gained 15.2% in Q2’26. It was the best quarterly performance since Q2’20. The key driver of the best June sector, Industrials gaining 7.29% in June and 20.15% YTD, is ISM Manufacturing PMI being above 50, which is expansion, every month in '26. It clearly shows a shift to sustained manufacturing from contraction.” See more great answers from our Foolish community TODAY’S QUESTION Thursday saw the latest Stock Advisor recommendation , Sterling Infrastructure, released! What's your take on companies that grow through acquisition ("roll-ups")? What separates a skillful acquirer that creates value from one that's just buying growth?
